routes.description: Establish that a beginningless temporal sequence is excluded either because concrete actual infinities are metaphysically impossible or because a temporal series cannot be formed by successive addition, while answering challenges based on temporal symmetry, tense, quantifier scope, and paradox reformulations.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if at least one independent philosophical argument supplies adequate grounds for a finite past and its indispensable premises remain applicable to temporal reality after the principal infinity, symmetry, and traversal objections are addressed.

motionBridge.description: Connect a defensible prohibition on a beginningless temporal sequence to adequate philosophical support for the claim that the universe began to exist.

centralBridges.description: Establish that the properties illustrated by concrete actual-infinity cases warrant excluding an actually infinite collection of past events.
Supply a principled difference between an instantiated beginningless past and an endless future that preserves the finite-past inference.
Establish that temporal accumulation cannot produce or traverse an actual infinite merely because every particular finite member is reachable.
Show that reverse-counting, Grim Reaper, Hilbert-style, or causal-finitist reasoning independently excludes a beginningless temporal or causal sequence.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Clarify the modal, tense, and distributive-versus-collective distinctions required by the central infinity arguments.
Explain why a beginningless process terminating at one finite point requires a non-arbitrary account of that endpoint.

routes.description: Withhold adequacy from the finite-past case by showing that counterintuitive infinite-set behavior does not establish impossibility, that past-future asymmetry is unsupported, and that successive-addition arguments conflate completion with memberwise coverage or rely on unresolved explanatory assumptions.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the principal actual-infinity and successive-addition arguments each retain an indispensable unsupported inference, equivocation, or symmetry problem, without requiring an independent demonstration that the universe is beginningless.

motionBridge.description: Show that the offered infinity arguments do not adequately establish a beginning of the universe, while bearing no burden to prove a beginningless universe.

centralBridges.description: Require a justified inference from unusual Cantorian consequences to metaphysical impossibility rather than treating counterintuitiveness as sufficient.
Show that the treatment of a beginningless past and endless future requires an independently defensible temporal symmetry breaker.
Distinguish every member being reached from a completed terminal act and require proof that the disputed every-to-all inference fails in the relevant case.
Challenge the sufficiency, endpoint-explanation, accumulation, or possibility premises used by reverse-counting and paradox-based finite-past arguments.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Keep simple-future, future-perfect, past, and present-existence claims aligned when testing purported temporal asymmetries.
Maintain the distinction between undermining the offered support for a beginning and affirmatively establishing a beginningless past.

sections.title: Actual Infinity: From Cantorian Consequences to Metaphysical Impossibility
sections.rationale: This issue tests the principal premise of the actual-infinity argument: whether Hilbert-style and related consequences justify excluding concrete actual infinities, or merely display familiar features of infinite collections.

sections.title: Past–Future Parity, Temporal Becoming, and Tense
sections.rationale: The finite-past inference depends on whether elapsed past events and unrealized future events differ in a way that blocks temporal mirroring without equivocating among present, future, and future-perfect claims.

sections.title: Successive Addition, Endless Counting, and Quantifier Scope
sections.rationale: This section contains the main clash over whether temporal succession can encompass every member of an infinite series, and whether memberwise reachability entails a collectively completed actual infinite.

sections.title: Beginningless Countdowns, Completion, and Endpoint Explanation
sections.rationale: Reverse-counting cases test whether infinitely much prior activity is sufficient for completion and whether a modest explanatory principle can exclude an otherwise arbitrary finishing point.

sections.title: Grim Reapers, Hilbert Reformulations, and Causal Finitism
sections.rationale: Alternative paradox and causal formulations matter because they may provide an independent finite-past route, but their force depends on possibility, accumulation, temporal-mirroring, and causal-structure premises.
